lenders_add.name: International Finance Corporation (IFC), through Indorama Kokand Textile and Hamkorbank
lenders_add.role: Senior A loan of up to US$40 million to Indorama Kokand Textile, a cotton yarn maker in the Fergana Valley, approved 17 December 2015 and fully disbursed 17 May 2016; and seven IFC equity, loan and trade-finance projects with Hamkorbank, an Andijan bank (US$13.5 million debt and US$5.3 million equity) (CAO).

sources_add.title: CAO Assessment Report: Indorama Kokand Textile and Hamkorbank, Uzbekistan

extend.note: Adds IFC. In June 2016 the International Labor Rights Forum, the Uzbek-German Forum, Human Rights Watch and the Cotton Campaign complained to CAO that forced labour was in Indorama Kokand's cotton supply chain and that Hamkorbank financed firms using it. During CAO's assessment, government employees told CAO that those who refused to pick had to pay substitute pickers or were threatened with job loss or loss of water, gas and electricity; monitor Elena Urlaeva reported being held in a psychiatric hospital in Tashkent from 1 to 23 March 2017 and detained by police in September and October 2017 (CAO). Through CAO mediation, joint monitoring by the parties during the 2021 harvest found no systemic forced or child labour in Indorama's supply fields; they settled in August 2022 and CAO closed the case in November 2024.

lenders_add.name: International Finance Corporation (IFC), through the Central American Mezzanine Infrastructure Fund (CAMIF)
lenders_add.role: IFC invested US$40 million in CAMIF in August 2009. CAMIF had approved and was actively considering an investment in Agua Zarca, but dropped it by December 2013; CAO found no other link between the developer DESA and IFC (CAO).

sources_add.title: CAO Assessment Report: Complaint regarding IFC's investment in CAMIF (Agua Zarca), Honduras

extend.note: Documents the IFC route the case's lender entry lacked. In October 2013 COPINH complained to CAO that Lenca ancestral land was taken for Agua Zarca without consultation and that the area had been militarised and Lenca leaders persecuted and criminalised, often with security forces involved. CAO closed the case in January 2014 because CAMIF was no longer considering the investment. Suggest the existing IFC lender entry and confidence_note be revised to say IFC's tie was through CAMIF's approved but abandoned investment, not a loan to the project.

Workplace pay and dismissal dispute. CAO's 2018 investigation is about termination pay for casual workers; it found no IFC compliance issue on union recognition, and the only force-related item is an April 2015 written warning of disciplinary action over strikes. CAO's report does record a company incident register of 15 injuries (Dec 2015-Feb 2016, four chemical splashes to eyes, one causing four days off work) and workers' accounts of slip-and-fall injuries, but CAO judged safety better than many Kenyan factories and found only that IFC lacked assurance; no serious injury, forced repression or harm to a community is documented. Complaints Bidco-04 (and Bidco-01) left as points, unlinked.
